whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer exam for?

personas.label: Marketing Cloud developers
personas.description: You write AMPscript, SSJS, and build CloudPages and want to certify your development skills.

personas.label: Email developers moving to Marketing Cloud
personas.description: You have HTML/CSS email experience and want to prove your ability to build dynamic, data-driven content in Marketing Cloud.

personas.label: Integration specialists
personas.description: You work with Marketing Cloud REST and SOAP APIs and want to validate your ability to build custom solutions and automations.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Engagement Developer exam is one of the harder Marketing Cloud certifications. It requires you to write and interpret AMPscript and SSJS code, understand REST and SOAP API patterns, and know how to build custom Journey Builder activities. Candidates without coding experience will struggle significantly.
bullets: ~67% passing score: standard for developer-level exams, but the technical depth makes it challenging.
Code interpretation required: expect questions that show AMPscript or SSJS snippets and ask you to predict the output or identify errors.
API knowledge tested: you must know REST and SOAP endpoint patterns, OAuth authentication, and when to use each API.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build at least 3-5 AMPscript-powered emails and 2-3 CloudPages before booking. Write SSJS Script Activities in Automation Studio and make at least a few REST API calls to feel confident.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 50-60% of questions are scenario-based. You’ll be asked to select the correct AMPscript function for a data retrieval task, choose between SSJS and AMPscript for a given use case, or design an API integration approach.
bestWayToPass: Master AMPscript data functions: Lookup, LookupRows, LookupOrderedRows, InsertData, and UpdateData are tested heavily. Know when to use each one.
Know SSJS vs AMPscript boundaries: Use AMPscript for email personalization, SSJS for complex logic and API calls in CloudPages and Script Activities.
Study REST API endpoints: Know the key /contacts/, /messaging/, and /data/ endpoint families and how OAuth 2.0 client credentials authentication works.
Practice CloudPages development: Build landing pages with form capture, personalized URLs, and dynamic content to prepare for hands-on scenario questions.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests hands-on coding in Marketing Cloud: writing AMPscript and SSJS, building CloudPages, calling REST and SOAP APIs, and creating custom Journey Builder activities. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Programmatic Languages (35%) and API (22%).

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: AMPscript Advanced Functions
blocks.body: Key AMPscript functions: Lookup() retrieves a single DE value; LookupRows() returns a full rowset; Row() and Field() navigate rowsets. FOR/NEXT loops iterate over rowsets. IIF() is the inline conditional; IF/ELSEIF/ENDIF for multi-branch logic. TreatAsContentArea() renders a content area by name. HTTPGet() and HTTPPost() call external APIs from AMPscript. DateAdd() and DateParse() handle date manipulation. The developer exam tests selecting the right function for a given personalisation or data retrieval scenario.

blocks.heading: Server-Side JavaScript (SSJS) in Marketing Cloud
blocks.body: SSJS runs on Marketing Cloud servers (not in the browser) using JavaScript 1.6 syntax. Platform functions (Marketing Cloud-specific) are available alongside standard JS. Common uses: HTTP POST to external systems, manipulating Data Extensions, complex data processing. SSJS runs in Email, Landing Pages, and Automation Studio Script activities. Key objects: Platform.Load(), HTTP.Post(), Retrieve(), DataExtension.Add(). The developer exam tests when to use SSJS vs AMPscript: SSJS for complex logic and API integration, AMPscript for personalisation within emails.

blocks.heading: CloudPages and Dynamic Content
blocks.body: CloudPages host landing pages, microsites, and smart capture forms. AMPscript-powered CloudPages can capture form data to Data Extensions (SmartCapture). Personalised URLs (PURLs) embed subscriber tokens in CloudPage URLs for pre-filled forms. Dynamic content blocks in emails show different content to different audiences based on rules, configured in Content Builder. The developer builds reusable content blocks with AMPscript logic for personalisation across campaigns.

blocks.heading: Marketing Cloud REST and SOAP APIs
blocks.body: **REST API**: subscriber management (POST /contacts/v1/contacts), Data Extension CRUD (/data/v1/async/dataextensions/), message send (/messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends/). **SOAP API**: Subscriber, List, TriggeredSend objects, legacy but still tested. Authentication: obtain access token via **OAuth** 2.0 client credentials flow, include Bearer token in API headers. The developer exam tests which API endpoint handles a given task and how to construct the request body.

blocks.heading: Automation Studio Script Activities
blocks.body: Script Activities run SSJS code within Automation Studio workflows. Common use cases: data manipulation between DE extracts, calling external APIs, complex data quality checks before sends. Script Activities run synchronously. Keep them under 30 minutes to avoid timeout. Error handling: use try/catch in SSJS; log errors to a dedicated error DE. The developer designs automation sequences combining Script Activities, SQL Query Activities, Data Extract Activities, and File Transfer Activities for complex data processing pipelines.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer exam tests technical development skills: AMPscript, SSJS, REST/SOAP APIs, and custom activities. Questions require you to write or interpret code snippets and design custom solutions.

blocks.heading: AMPscript Proficiency
blocks.body: Master AMPscript data functions: Lookup, LookupRows, LookupOrderedRows, UpdateData, InsertData. Know conditional logic (IIF, CASE), date/string functions, and how to use AMPscript in subject lines, preheaders, and email body.

blocks.heading: Server-Side JavaScript (SSJS)
blocks.body: Know SSJS for CloudPages and landing page logic: using Platform.Load to import functions, Core.JavaScript library for data extensions (Rows, Row objects), and how SSJS differs from client-side JavaScript.

blocks.heading: REST & SOAP API Usage
blocks.body: Know the key Marketing Cloud **REST API** endpoints: /contacts/v1/contacts, /messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends, /data/v1/async, and how to authenticate using **OAuth** 2.0 client credentials.

blocks.heading: Custom Activities in Journey Builder
blocks.body: Know how to build custom Journey Builder activities using the Custom Activity API: the config.json structure, execute/save/publish/validate endpoints, and how activities interact with Journey Builder's UI.

blocks.heading: Query Activities & Data Extensions
blocks.body: Know how to write SQL in Automation Studio Query Activities to transform and aggregate data extension data. Understand overwrite vs. append destination actions and how to join data extensions in queries.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer needs to retrieve a value from a data extension and use it in an email. Which AMPscript function does this?
options: RaiseError, which stops processing for the subscriber being rendered
Lookup
SystemDateToLocalDate, which converts a stored date into local time
InsertData, which writes a new row into the target data extension instead
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lookup returns a single field value from a data extension row matching the criteria supplied.
whyWrong: RaiseError halts the send for that subscriber.
That function performs date conversion.
InsertData writes rather than reads.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main reason to use SSJS rather than AMPscript in a Marketing Cloud build?
options: It is the only language able to read from a sendable data extension
It renders more quickly than AMPscript does during a large email send
It is required whenever an email contains more than one content block
It handles loops, objects and API calls more comfortably
sampleQuestions.explanation: Server-Side JavaScript suits logic with real data structures, iteration and platform API work, where AMPscript becomes awkward.
whyWrong: AMPscript reads data extensions perfectly well.
AMPscript is generally the faster choice for inline personalisation.
Content block count has nothing to do with the language.

sampleQuestions.question: A cloud page must accept a form post and write it to a data extension. What should the developer be most careful about?
options: Validating and encoding the submitted input
Confirming that the data extension has a retention policy configured on it
Ensuring the page is published to the correct content folder in the account
Checking that the page uses the same template as the rest of the site
sampleQuestions.explanation: A public endpoint accepting user input needs validation and encoding, or it becomes an injection and data integrity problem.
whyWrong: Retention matters for storage, not for accepting input safely.
Folder location is housekeeping rather than a safety concern.
Template consistency is a presentation detail.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a triggered send definition provide?
options: A reusable configuration for sending one message on demand
A journey entry source that evaluates a data extension every hour
A report showing which subscribers received a particular email send
A schedule that causes an email to be sent at a fixed time each day
sampleQuestions.explanation: Triggered sends are set up once and then invoked, usually via the API, to send a single message to one subscriber immediately.
whyWrong: Entry source evaluation is a Journey Builder setting.
Send reporting is produced by tracking.
Scheduled sending is configured in Automation Studio.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer must call the Marketing Cloud REST API from an external system. What is needed first?
options: A data extension marked as sendable and related to subscribers
An access token obtained from the auth endpoint
A cloud page published with a public URL for the system to call
A triggered send definition created and published in the account
sampleQuestions.explanation: REST calls are authenticated with a token obtained from the authentication endpoint using the installed package credentials.
whyWrong: Sendable extensions matter for sends, not for authenticating.
Cloud pages are a different integration surface.
Triggered sends are one thing you might call, not a prerequisite.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of an installed package in Marketing Cloud?
options: It schedules the automations that run overnight in the account
It defines the retention rules applied to each data extension
It holds the credentials and scope for API access
It stores the email templates shared between the business units
sampleQuestions.explanation: Installed packages carry the client credentials and the permission scopes that an integration is granted.
whyWrong: Scheduling is configured in Automation Studio.
Retention is set per data extension.
Templates live in Content Builder.

sampleQuestions.question: A SQL query in Automation Studio must combine subscriber data with send history. Where does the send data come from?
options: Data views exposed within the account
A data extension that the developer creates and populates by hand
The tracking tab on each of the individual email jobs that were sent
The All Subscribers list filtered to the relevant date range
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data views such as _Sent, _Open and _Click expose send and engagement history to queries.
whyWrong: Manual population would be unmaintainable and immediately stale.
Per-job tracking is a user interface view, not a queryable source.
All Subscribers holds status rather than send history.

sampleQuestions.question: Why must a developer be careful with a SQL query that has no filter on date?
options: It can scan far more data than it needs to
Queries without a date filter are rejected by the platform automatically
The results will be written to the wrong target data extension instead
Data views only return rows from the current calendar month in any case
sampleQuestions.explanation: Unbounded queries over large data views are slow and can time out, so constraining the period is basic hygiene.
whyWrong: The platform does not reject them outright.
The target is set in the activity regardless of the filter.
Data views hold a longer history than one month.

sampleQuestions.question: What happens to an AMPscript error during a send?
options: The send is paused until a developer corrects the error in the content
The entire send is cancelled and no subscriber receives the email at all
The email is sent with the failing block silently omitted from the content
That subscriber's message fails while others continue
sampleQuestions.explanation: AMPscript is evaluated per subscriber, so a failure affects that individual message rather than the whole job.
whyWrong: Sends are not paused for developer intervention.
A single failure does not cancel the send.
The message fails rather than rendering partially.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer needs the same personalisation logic in twelve emails. What is the maintainable approach?
options: A cloud page that each of the emails links out to when it is opened
A shared content block containing the logic
The same code pasted into each of the twelve individual email templates
A separate triggered send definition created for each of the emails
sampleQuestions.explanation: A shared block is referenced by each email, so the logic is written and corrected in one place.
whyWrong: Sending readers to a web page is not personalisation of the email.
Twelve copies means twelve places to fix every bug.
Triggered sends are about sending, not sharing logic.

sampleQuestions.question: What distinguishes a sendable data extension from a non-sendable one?
options: It is permitted to hold more rows than a non-sendable extension can
It is visible to every business unit configured within the account
It is backed up automatically each night by the platform itself
It is related to subscribers so it can be used as an audience
sampleQuestions.explanation: Marking an extension sendable and mapping its relationship to subscribers is what allows it to be targeted by a send.
whyWrong: Row capacity is not affected by the sendable flag.
Visibility is governed by business unit and folders.
Backups are not a function of being sendable.

sampleQuestions.question: A journey must be entered by a single contact when an external system says so. What should the developer use?
options: A data extension entry source re-evaluated once every fifteen minutes
An automation that imports a file each time the external system changes
An API event entry source
A triggered send definition invoked directly by the external system
sampleQuestions.explanation: API events let an external system inject one contact into a journey in real time.
whyWrong: A re-evaluated extension is still batch and introduces delay.
File-based import is slower and more fragile than an event.
A triggered send sends a message rather than entering a journey.

sampleQuestions.question: Why would a developer store configuration values in a data extension rather than in the code?
options: The platform imposes a strict limit on the length of any AMPscript block
They can be changed without editing and republishing content
Data extensions are able to execute the logic that uses those values
Values held in a data extension are encrypted by the platform by default
sampleQuestions.explanation: Externalising values means a marketer or admin can change behaviour without a developer touching the content.
whyWrong: Block length is not the reason to externalise configuration.
Data extensions store data; they do not execute logic.
There is no automatic encryption of ordinary stored values.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer is asked to make an email render differently for subscribers in two countries. What is the simplest approach?
options: Two separate emails, each one sent to its own country segment
A cloud page that detects the recipient's location when they open it
Conditional content driven by a country attribute
Two triggered send definitions, one configured for each of the countries
sampleQuestions.explanation: Conditional logic on an attribute you already hold keeps it to a single asset with one place to maintain.
whyWrong: Two emails doubles the maintenance for the same outcome.
Detecting location on open is unreliable and happens too late.
Triggered sends do not solve a content variation problem.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best describes the developer's role in a Marketing Cloud implementation?
options: Deciding which audiences each of the marketing campaigns should target
Designing the visual layout and copy used in each of the email templates
Building the data, logic and integrations behind the campaigns
Managing the account's sending reputation and deliverability over time
sampleQuestions.explanation: The developer builds the plumbing: data models, queries, personalisation logic, cloud pages and API integrations that campaigns run on.
whyWrong: Audience strategy is a marketing decision.
Visual design and copy sit with the marketing team.
Deliverability is usually an operational or consulting responsibility.
